cases.article:
Interpreting an Extraction Audit
In this fictional audit of 400 randomly selected contract passages, an extractor made 20 field errors; no error-cause investigation was conducted.
The observed fraction of passages with one field error was five percent; each affected passage had exactly one field error.
These 20 errors prove that ambiguous annotation instructions caused every error.
The overall exact-match accuracy was 95%, while recall for the critical termination-date field was 60%.
The system meets the required termination-date recall of at least 90% because overall accuracy exceeds 90%.
We should inspect the errors and report results for critical fields separately before drawing causal or deployment conclusions.

Which Adapter Was Tested?
This fictional release record says the independent evaluation tested adapter A with checksum aaaa and prompt template P1.
The candidate now proposed for release is adapter B with checksum bbbb and prompt template P2; no tests of this combination are recorded.
Because both files are named final_adapter, adapter A results certify adapter B and P2 without another evaluation.
Matching the filenames guarantees identical model weights and outputs.
A reviewer should bind evidence to the tested weights, base model, prompt template and evaluation configuration before recommending release.
